places.name: Arkansas River
places.note: Messy crossing scatters the herd; Wilbarger's bloodied horse waits on the north bank, and he dies beneath its bank.

places.raw_name: a few miles north of the Arkansas
places.name: Kansas
places.note: On ungrazed grass well west of Dodge, Call leaves Dish in charge of the herd and Lorena to ride to Wilbarger.
places.location_hint: a few miles north of the Arkansas River, west of Dodge City

places.name: Wilbarger's grave on the Arkansas
places.note: Wilbarger, shot three times by horsethieves, dies talking with the partners; they bury him under a buffalo skull.
places.location_hint: on the bank of the Arkansas River about ten miles east-southeast of the herd's crossing, west of Dodge City

places.name: Lonesome Dove
places.note: Wilbarger rode his big bay into it months earlier and still laughs about Augustus's sign.
places.location_hint: south Texas border town on the Rio Grande

places.name: Dodge City
places.note: Augustus doubts any herd has been trailed this far west of it.

places.name: Fort Worth
places.note: Wilbarger says the Suggs brothers are known there as murderers.

places.name: Hudson River
places.note: Wilbarger was born on it and expected to die there; his Virgil reminds him of it.

places.name: New York
places.note: His lawyer brother John lives there; Wilbarger asks that horse money be sent to him on Broadway.

places.name: Boston
places.note: Wilbarger says even a surgeon from there couldn't fix his lung.

places.name: Yale College
places.note: Augustus remarks Wilbarger is likely the only Yale man buried under a buffalo skull.

places.name: Nebraska
places.note: Lorena fears Gus may slip off to the woman there.

places.name: Europe
places.note: Augustus has heard its ground is so full of old bones you can't dig without finding some.

groups.label: Hat Creek herd under Dish
groups.hint: a few miles north of the Arkansas River crossing, west of Dodge City; Lorena's tent kept near the wagon

groups.label: Call's pursuit party
groups.hint: riding out at night from the grave, about ten miles from the herd, to follow the horsethieves' trail
